inc-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool 'dp-acme-prod' node gpu-32a reported NODE_DOWN by node-monitor. Immediate customer impact possible for pool-bound tenants. page: #oncall-elena

elena (oncall): acked — I'm on it. grabbing logs and routing table. tagging @matt for infra assist.

matt (infra): on my way. can you paste the node health output? I want to see GPU errors vs OS/kernel panic.

elena (oncall): pasted from node-monitor: `NODE_ID=gpu-32a STATUS=UNREACHABLE last_heartbeat=2025-11-02T03:41:12Z err=nvlink_timeout`

elena (oncall): perf-metrics show increased 503s for AcmeCorp tenants in dp-acme-prod starting 03:42Z. rate ~3% of requests, latency spikes for small gen workloads.

jess (cust-success): pinging Acme primary contact (S. Lee) now to confirm visible customer impact. will say we are investigating and will provide 10m updates.

ryan (sre): checking pool routing. looks like the pool has 12 nodes; 1 node down should not cause >1% errors ordinarily. seeing some requests still pinned to gpu-32a — maybe KV cache sticky sessions.

matt (infra): run `rctl node status --pool dp-acme-prod --node gpu-32a`
matt (infra): output: ```
node: gpu-32a
state: UNREACHABLE
last_ssh: 2025-11-02T03:40:59Z
gpu_err: ECC_CORRECTABLE_UNRECOVERABLE
attached_tenants: [acme-frontend, acme-billing, internal-test]
current_sessions: 18
```

elena (oncall): current_sessions 18 explains the sticky failures. plan: cordon node, start live drain (evict sessions) to fallback nodes in same pool, enable bypass routing to dp-acme-fallback if drain stalls >5m.

matt (infra): attempting graceful drain: `rctl drain-node --pool dp-acme-prod --node gpu-32a --mode graceful --timeout 300`
matt (infra): initial evict log: ```
evicting tenant acme-frontend session 1023 -> migrated to gpu-27b
evicting tenant acme-billing session 79 -> migrated to gpu-09c
error evicting internal-test session 5: pinned_kv_active
```

ryan (sre): internal-test is a long-running job from our QA run; we can force-evict but that risks killing a process. suggest we prioritize customer-facing tenants first (acme-frontend, acme-billing) and postpone internal-test eviction until we have replacement capacity.

jess (cust-success): Acme says they see errors in billing flow now. they asked if we can failover them to the fallback pool ASAP. They are on a dedicated contract and prefer no visible disruption.

matt (infra): enabling bypass routing for acme-frontend and acme-billing to dp-acme-fallback: `rctl routing override --tenant acme-frontend,acme-billing --from dp-acme-prod --to dp-acme-fallback --ttl 1800`
matt (infra): override applied. watching logs.

elena (oncall): update: 503s for Acme dropped to ~0.2% within 45s of override. billing flow test from Acme contact shows success for 3 consecutive calls.

inc-bot: INCIDENT: Severity assigned SEV2 (target: 1h mitigation) — reason: enterprise tenant (AcmeCorp) experiencing degraded service on dedicated pool.

aaron (hardware): ECC unrecoverable on GPU 0 suggests possible hardware degradation. if this is a failing GPU we should replace the instance. check with cloud provider for hot-replacement or host reboot.

matt (infra): opening provider ticket: `CLOUD-TICKET-987654`: "Instance gpu-32a reporting ECC_UNRECOVERABLE; request host remediation or instance reprovision." ETA provider initial response 20m.

ryan (sre): since we have fallback routing in place for the customer-facing tenants and errors are down, next steps: 1) keep node cordoned 2) continue eviction attempts for remaining sessions with `--force` if provider confirms replacement will take >10m 3) if it's a spot interruption, we need to mark pool as degraded and consider moving more tenants to dp-acme-warm.

elena (oncall): trying a force drain for internal-test after confirming it's non-customer critical: `rctl drain-node --pool dp-acme-prod --node gpu-32a --mode force`
matt (infra): force evict succeeded; current_sessions 0. node is now cordoned and drained from scheduler perspective.

ops-scheduler-bot: scheduled action: `reprovision-node --pool dp-acme-prod --node gpu-32a --when now` (job id 7862).

aaron (hardware): provider replied to ticket: "Host unrecoverable; instance will be replaced within 12-18 minutes. No data loss expected. If immediate replacement required, we can cold-migrate."

matt (infra): since node is drained, I'm OK waiting for provider replacement. marking node for reprovision and will monitor for stray kube-proxies.

jess (cust-success): updated Acme: we’ve routed their production traffic off the impacted node, drained the node, and provider is replacing the host. We expect no further customer-visible errors. They requested a post-incident summary and timeline.

elena (oncall): handing over to @matt for infra follow-up and hardware ticket tracking. I'm switching to next rotation in 15m but will stay available for escalation. @matt please set incident owner in system and add runbook link `docs/runbooks/dedicated-node-failure`.

matt (infra): taking owner. I created follow-up ticket INFRA-2103 to track replacement and postmortem. Will collect NVML logs and attach.

ryan (sre): quick notes for postmortem: 1) why sticky sessions remained pinned despite our cache invalidation 2) consider auto-bypass when node_health==UNREACHABLE and active_sessions < threshold 3) test warm standby scale-up for dedicated pools to avoid potential 503 windows.

elena (oncall): ack. adding to incident notes. Also flagging that this pool uses a mix of preemptible/spot and reserved instances — need clearer routing or capacity padding for enterprise tenants.

inc-bot: STATUS UPDATE scheduled at +10m and +60m.

matt (infra): provider completed replacement at 1750002200. reprovisioning completed and node rejoined as gpu-32a at 1750002285. performing healthcheck: `rctl node health --pool dp-acme-prod --node gpu-32a` -> `OK`

elena (oncall): confirmed cluster health stable. removed routing override for acme-frontend/acme-billing: `rctl routing remove-override --id <override-id>`

jess (cust-success): told Acme their traffic has been returned to normal and shared timeline. they asked for the postmortem and to confirm if this was a spot eviction or hardware failure. I said we'll confirm after infra's NVML logs.

matt (infra): NVML logs indicate ECC unrecoverable error on GPU 0 — hardware fault, not spot eviction. attaching logs to INFRA-2103. recommending retiring this host from the pool for now and reimage with known-good GPU.

aaron (hardware): ordering replacement hardware through provider escalation channel (noting it's a hardware failure).

elena (oncall): closing this handoff. follow-ups: INFRA-2103 (replacement and logs), PM-ACME-OUTAGE (customer summary), and POSTMORTEM-789 (root cause and action items). I'll mark incident resolved in 30m if no regression.

inc-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status=mitigated owner=matt( infra ) severity=SEV2

matt (infra): final note: we should add a routing rule: if node_health==UNREACHABLE and drain_success==false within 120s then auto-route customer tenants to fallback pool to minimize impact. created RFC in rfc/pool-failover.

elena (oncall): thanks all. good coordination.

jess (cust-success): confirmed Acme happy with immediate mitigation. they'll expect the postmortem and SLO credit evaluation if warranted.

inc-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED at 1750002350 (mitigated, follow-ups filed).
